audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3..6].side read Skill while win[3..6] read Xerath and the packet chart reads Xerath on all seven rows.
audit.why: 47.92% over 1686 games with a permanent range deficit — Xerath holds every row. Two layers were rendering different answers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as pure range dominance with no mention of what Rite of the Arcane costs him.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Xerath immobilizes himself' for the barrage, and the kit flags it channel/interruptible on 130/115/100s. That is the one moment he cannot move.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] and whys[4] now state the self-root and the 130s cooldown, and that Flash Frost cancels the channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interaction errors: 'Eye of Destruction stacks/charges' (the W has no stacking mechanic), 'use minions as cover to block incoming Arcanopulse' (Q hits all targets in its path, so minions are not cover), and no mention anywhere that his R is an interruptible channel.
audit.why: Riot text for Q is 'a long-range beam of energy, dealing magic damage to all targets hit' — piercing, not single-target. W 'calls down a barrage… slowing and dealing damage', a one-shot zone. E 'deals magic damage to an enemy and stuns them' — a projectile that stops on the first unit, so THAT is what minions block. R is flagged channel.
audit.corrected: Minion cover moved to Shocking Orb; W described as a slow that sets up the orb; R channel-cancel stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere (sequencingCues 0).
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and is his only CC; Rite of the Arcane is 130s at rank 1. Those two numbers are the whole timing model of the lane.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with both numbers and the wait-for-X-then-Y structure.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Xerath wins by slowing you with Eye of Destruction, landing Shocking Orb, and finishing from off your screen.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Crystallize like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb: 13s at rank 1 and his only CC — it stops on the first unit, so keep a minion between you; with it down the artillery never converts. - Rite of the Arcane is 130s at rank 1 and a channel your Flash Frost cancels outright.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the one moment he stands still: Rite of the Arcane roots him for the channel, and a stun there ends it.

edits.before: Xerath whiffs Shocking Orb (Stun) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: With the orb on cooldown he has no CC — walk up and wall his path home.

edits.before: That is Xerath’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Your Q costs 80 mana; Mana Surge refunds his poke for free.

edits.before: Your wall is your Flash — a wasted Crystallize means the next gank kills the bird AND the egg.
edits.after: Arcanopulse pierces every minion in the line — cover does not exist against his Q, only distance.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Xerath walks straight at you.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane reaches 5000 units — with the egg down, being anywhere on his half of the map is the danger.

edits.before: Level 3: Eye of Destruction stacks begin adding to his poke damage, widening his lead as Anivia's combo still can't reach him.
edits.after: Level 3: Eye of Destruction adds a 1000-range slow that sets up Shocking Orb, widening his lead while your combo cannot reach.

edits.before: Level 6: Rite of the Arcane hits from a range Anivia's Glacial Storm can never match, keeping Xerath's advantage intact through the power spike.
edits.after: Level 6: Rite of the Arcane fires at 5000 range while he stands rooted in place — he keeps the edge unless you are close enough to stun the channel.

edits.before: Xerath's Arcanopulse-Eye of Destruction poke outranges your Flash Frost setup entirely, letting him chip you down without ever entering your combo range.
edits.after: Arcanopulse pierces the whole minion line and Eye of Destruction slows you into Shocking Orb, chipping you down from outside your combo range.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane out-damages your Glacial Storm at a range you can never close, keeping his lead firmly intact.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane roots him in place for the channel — 130s at rank 1, and your Flash Frost cancels it outright.

edits.before: Anivia is at a fundamental range disadvantage from level 1 — Xerath's poke starts outranging your Flash Frost setup immediately and only gets worse as he stacks Eye of Destruction charges through levels 3-5. There's no real engage window here since walking into his poke range to set up Q just eats more damage than you can trade back. Farm patiently from max range, use minions for cover, and don't contest CS he's willing to zone you off of.
edits.after: Anivia is at a fundamental range disadvantage from level 1 — Xerath's poke starts outranging your Flash Frost setup immediately, and by 3-5 Eye of Destruction slows you into a 13s Shocking Orb for free. There's no real engage window here since walking into his poke range to set up Q just eats more damage than you can trade back. Farm patiently from max range, body-block the orb with a minion, and don't contest CS he's willing to zone you off of.

edits.before: Use minions as cover to block incoming Arcanopulse
edits.after: Keep a minion between you and his Shocking Orb stun

edits.before: Poke relentlessly from max range with Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction stacks
edits.after: Poke from max range with Arcanopulse, then slow her with Eye of Destruction

notes: Two real mechanical errors killed: Eye of Destruction has no stacks or charges (it is a single barrage that slows), and minions do NOT block Arcanopulse — Riot's text says it damages all targets hit. Minion cover works against Shocking Orb, which stops on the first unit, so the advice was pointed at the wrong ability. Added the R-is-a-channel interaction from _missing. Level chart squared to all-Xerath across both layers, matching the packet and the 47.92% win rate. | COHERENCE: 4 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
